channel.title: Stobox
channel.description: Real-world asset tokenization, written as the work happened.

item.title: The Investor-Ready Company: Why AI and Tokenization Now Decide Who Raises Capital in 2026
item.description: In 2026 the fundraising bottleneck moved from access to trust. AI diligence and tokenized securities both reward the same thing: structured, verifiable, investor-ready data. Here is why legibility, not pitch, now decides who raises.

item.title: The Wrapper Decides: Why Tokenized Asset Structuring, Not Minting, Determines Institutional Liquidity in 2026
item.description: The RWA market crossed $36B on-chain, but most tokens barely trade. The decision that separates a liquid digital security from an inert one is made before the first token is minted: the legal wrapper.

item.title: The SEC Wants to Let the Blockchain Be the Official Share Register
item.description: On September 1, 2026 the SEC proposed the first rewrite of its transfer agent rules in over 40 years. For the first time, a blockchain could serve as the official record of who owns a security. Here is what the 421-page proposal actually says, in plain language – and why Stobox has been building for exactly this moment since 2018.

item.title: The Data-Ready Company: Why Enterprise AI Agents Fail on Foundations, Not Intelligence
item.description: Enterprise AI agents do not fail because models are weak. They fail because the data underneath them is unstructured, ungoverned, and unverified. In 2026, data readiness is the dividing line between the companies that scale AI and the 95% that stall.

item.title: The Agent-Ready Raise: How AI and Tokenization Are Rewriting Capital Formation
item.description: AI agents are moving from research tools to autonomous capital-market participants, and tokenized private assets crossed $22B. The companies that raise capital next will be the ones whose data machines can read, verify, and act on.

item.title: The RWA Liquidity Illusion: Why Tokenized Assets Sit Idle in 2026
item.description: On-chain RWA value quadrupled to $33.5B, yet most of it never trades. The real 2026 story is not issuance. It is usability: the assets that can be traded, posted as collateral, and settled are the ones winning.

item.title: Stobox Weekly RWA & Tokenization Digest: August 19–25, 2026
item.description: Coinbase put tokenized US stocks live on Base with the new B20 standard, Standard Chartered became the first bank to distribute Hong Kong's HKDAP stablecoin, and the RWA market held near $38.4B as holders topped 2.5M. The week the equity race and the settlement layer both moved.

item.title: The Agent-Ready Company: Why Autonomous AI Fails Without Data It Can Act On
item.description: Enterprises are moving from copilots to autonomous agents in 2026. The binding constraint is no longer model quality: it is whether your business data and context are structured enough for an agent to act on. Here is what separates the companies that scale.

item.title: Tokenizing Real Estate the Legal Way: Why Liens Beat Fractionalizing the House
item.description: Naive LLC-wrapper fractionalization of a home collides with US property and securities law. The cleaner path may be tokenizing county-recorded instruments: the mortgage note and lien, not the deed.

item.title: The Capital Bifurcation: Why 90% of Fundraisers Need New Rails in 2026
item.description: Five mega-firms captured 73% of new private-capital commitments in H1 2026. The other 90% of fundraisers are being priced out of traditional pools. Tokenized, investor-ready infrastructure is becoming their only viable alternative.

item.title: RWA Tokenization in 2026: The $38B Market Is Concentrated in the Wrong Place
item.description: Tokenized real-world assets crossed $38B in 2026, but nearly all of it sits in Treasuries and cash. The real opportunity in private markets is barely on-chain, and the reason is infrastructure, not demand.

item.title: Stobox Weekly RWA & Tokenization Digest: August 12–18, 2026
item.description: The week Washington wrote the rules: Treasury proposed GENIUS Act stablecoin rules, the SEC delayed its tokenization exemption again, and Ondo Stocks crossed $1B as the RWA market pressed toward $40B.

item.title: Financing What Doesn't Exist Yet: Stobox, Economy of Trust Ukraine, and the Capital Path for Reconstruction
item.description: Ukraine's reconstruction is an €800 billion+ need with a structural financing gap at the earliest stage: nobody funds the proving phase, because early capital has no path back to liquidity. Economy of Trust Ukraine built the governance architecture; Stobox provides the tokenization infrastructure that gives the earliest money a defined exit. Here is how the two fit together.

item.title: What Is Stobox? The Company, the Stack, and How Tokenization Actually Gets Done
item.description: Stobox is an infrastructure layer for tokenized capital markets: one company, three products, eight years of doing the unglamorous work between a real-world asset and a regulated on-chain security. This is the canonical explainer – what Stobox is, what each layer of the stack does, what it costs, and what Stobox deliberately is not.

item.title: The AI ROI Gap Is a Data Problem: Why 95% of Enterprise AI Pilots Fail
item.description: Enterprises poured $30-40B into generative AI and 95% of pilots returned nothing. The dividing line is not model quality. It is whether the company's data and workflows are AI-ready.

item.title: Permissioned Blockchains for Finance: Where Wall Street's Regulated Capital Flows First
item.description: Large pools of regulated capital demand surveilled, compliant environments. That is why institutional RWA flows are landing on permissioned chains and permissioned layers on public rails, not on open DeFi. Here is where the money is actually going, and how to build for it.

item.title: The RWA Liquidity Gap: Why $33 Billion in Tokenized Assets Still Can't Trade
item.description: Tokenized real-world assets tripled to $33.5B in a year, but most of that value sits idle. The winners of the next phase will build tradeable secondary markets, not bigger issuance numbers.

item.title: Our Reg D Seed Round Is Open, and It Carries TigerMark Coverage
item.description: The US leg of the Stobox seed round is live on Silicon Prairie, open to verified accredited investors. We have also secured TigerMark, a D&O and securities-liability policy built for regulated online offerings. Here is what it is, and what it deliberately is not.

item.title: Stobox Weekly RWA & Tokenization Digest: August 5–11, 2026
item.description: Tokenized RWAs hit $38.17B and closed within $1.83B of the $40B milestone as holders jumped 56% to 1.7M. Tether took real estate tokenization to Saudi Arabia, Binance's bStocks seized 85% of tokenized-equity DEX volume, and the GENIUS Act rulebook slipped to 2027.

item.title: The AI Data Divide: Why Your Company's Data Decides Whether AI (and Investors) Trust You

item.description: Tokenized RWA has crossed $34B to $51B depending on who counts, yet most of it never trades. The bottleneck is not the blockchain. It is the structuring decisions made before the first token is minted.
